newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen rally may hit speed bump at 112.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen rally may hit speed bump at 112.

text.p: The dollar may encounter difficulty near term conquering the key psychological barrier of 112 yen, but the medium-term outlook still calls for a test of the 113 to 113.50 area, chartists said.

On Monday, the U.S. unit soared briefly to 111.68 yen, a 32-week high. U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated support for a strong dollar, while Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said the Japanese economy is in a slow recovery.
"I think we could go a little bit higher short-term, maybe we see 112 (yen)," said David Solin, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.

"But again, I think we're at the point where people are going to start to get a little nervous," Solin said. "They're going to see these major new highs and not any kind of significant follow through."
In late New York dealings, the dollar traded around 111.35 yen, down from 111.50/60 yen at the opening.

Chartists agreed the dollar faces little in the way of technical resistance between where it is currently trading and 113 to 113.50/60 yen. "Once we got through that 111.20, there is really nothing between here and there," said Mary Beth Slack, a foreign exchange analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.
However, Slack deemed 112 yen a near-term target, adding that "they'll be looking for the market to sell out at 112."
She said the worst-case scenario for dollar/yen would be to slip back to 110.70, a level of coincident support.
But even if the dollar corrected lower, chartists still expect the U.S. currency to resume its climb.
Slack emphasized the market is more biased for dollar calls than it is for dollar puts.
"That means that people ... are starting to get ideas the market is going to continue much, much higher from here," she said.
As for predicting when the dollar might hit the 113.0 to 113.50/60 yen area, chartists estimates ranged from about two to six weeks.
The dollar ended slightly weaker on Monday, closing at 1.5246/51 marks compared with 1.5272/77 at the opening.
Solin said the dollar could surpass an earlier high at 1.5290 marks, climb to 1.5310/20 and sell-off again.
"The net short-term trend is slightly higher but generally these are more topping patterns," he added.
